stories.title: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.3 Image Klein trends on Hugging Face
stories.summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.3 Image Klein, an open-weight image-to-image model, is trending on Hugging Face with over 46,000 downloads and 459 likes.
stories.more: FLUX.3 Image Klein is an image-to-image model from Black Forest Labs, distributed on Hugging Face in safetensors format for use with the diffusers library. It has drawn 459 likes and more than 46,000 downloads, placing it among Hugging Face's trending models. The listing categorizes it under image generation and image editing. Further technical details, such as parameter count or training data, were not included in the listing.

stories.title: Opencode suffers security breach, users urged to rotate API keys
stories.summary: A Reddit report says the AI coding tool Opencode has been breached, with users advised to rotate their API keys as a precaution.
stories.more: A post on r/LocalLLaMA reported that Opencode, an AI coding tool, has suffered a security breach. The post urges users to rotate their API keys as a precaution. Details of the breach were still developing at the time of the report, and no information was given about its scope, cause, or how many users are affected.

stories.title: Anthropic says its workforce is less junior, spends more time in meetings
stories.summary: Anthropic says the composition of its workforce and the nature of its work have shifted significantly over the past year, with fewer junior staff and more meeting time.
stories.more: TechCrunch reported that Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior over the past year. The company also said employees are spending more time in meetings than before. According to the report, the composition of Anthropic's workforce and the type of work being done have changed significantly in that period. No further detail on the size of the shift or its causes was given in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Simon Willison highlights a document.currentScript inline-rendering trick
stories.summary: Simon Willison shared a technique by Lean Rada that uses document.currentScript to create a tiny inline templating trick in JavaScript.
stories.more: Simon Willison linked to a post by Lean Rada describing a trick that uses the document.currentScript property in JavaScript. The technique lets a script tag replace itself with computed content when the page loads, such as inserting the current year. Willison notes that defining a short helper function turns this into a minimal templating language. The post is tagged under JavaScript on Willison's blog.

items.title: Inline rendering with document​.currentScript
items.excerpt: Inline rendering with document​.currentScript Lean Rada describes a neat trick that takes advantage of the document.currentScript property. You can use that to drop in a tiny inline element that replaces itself when the page loads: The year is document.currentScript.replaceWith( new Date().getFullYear()) If you define a shortcut function like this: $=(...n)=>document.currentScript.replaceWith(...n) You get a tiny template language: The year is $(new Date().getFullYear()) Tags: javascript
